The London, Hyde Park, protest, from the POV of someone who was actually there (ofc I can’t talk on behalf of the thousands that were there) but I need everyone to understand how the media is twisting this movement and still forcing racist stereotypes on the black community ~

It was calm & peaceful, we remained in Hyde Park for a while as we had John Boyega & Belly Mujingas family come and talk to us to raise awareness and to not let the victims names be forgotten they were overwhelmed with the amount of support and the amount of people who showed up

Black lives matter, black futures matter, black dreams matter, do not stop fighting for these people, use your voices, use your platforms, we will never understand the horror they have been through and continue to go through but we can stand with them (3/3)

We marched from Hyde Park through to downing street (where our Prime Minister resides) some people departed at the US embassy, some at Parliment, we stopped traffic, cars were supporting us, WE WERE PEACEFUL, we walked, we chanted, we asked for justice

Not a single person was pushing and shoving, everyone stood still, everyone chanted, everyone joined in, everyone was there for the same reason, we want justice, we want to remember the victims of such brutal force, we want to be heard and I want to amplify their voices

There were so many different chants today for so many different reasons, we were PROMISED by police officers that no one would get arrested if we remained peaceful, we had our rights read to us and we were all given numbers to call if anything happened

We remembered so many victims today, we screamed their names begging for the world to change its ways, black skin should not be a death sentence, black skin is not a crime, stop grouping, stop stereotyping, stop the racism

Things like this need to be documented, because I hadn’t even left the protest yet when I saw and heard that the media was ONLY focused on reporting the small part of violence that happened right at the end, nothing to do with the 6.5 hours proir to that, it was peaceful

Endless chanting, we made sure we were heard, we marched from Hyde Park and on the way down to downing street, we stopped by westminster station where there were more speakers, more people showing support and using their voices

Sometimes everyone stopped to take an 8 minute silence, sometimes we stopped to kneel, sometimes we stopped to just cheer and create as much noise as possible, I cannot stress enough how united this whole movement was today, and how peaceful it remained through most of it

Crowds showed up, there were thousands of us, all marching together to show the importance of this movement and how much the justice system needs to change, no one has ever said “fuck the fire department” because they’ve not done anything wrong
This was around the time the violence was happening, on the same street just the other end, so DO NOT let the media fool you into thinking this whole protest was a violent riot from start to finish

Yes there was a small moment of violence in this protest which of course shouldnt have happened, but by the time i’d heard about it, me & a girl I met there had already left, despite it happening on the same street we were at, we didn’t hear or see it ourselves, so it was a shock
